articles.title: Every GTA Game Ranked
articles.summary: With the arrival of GTA 6, IGN has ranked every Grand Theft Auto game Rockstar ever released from worst to best. Which GTA game did IGN crown as the best? Check out our list below.
articles.body:
From Liberty City to San Andreas, Rockstar has built a rich world of career criminals, lunatics, and thieves, and we’ve loved each and every one. Although over 25 years old, the record-breaking views on the first Grand Theft Auto 6 trailer is proof that Rockstar’s iconic game series remains one of the most popular franchises on the planet.

From humble beginnings — the series originally began as top-down car-stealing games — to creating some of the most advanced and realistic open world games in the industry, each new Grand Theft Auto game is worthy of celebration. So, with Grand Theft Auto 6 on the horizon, IGN has thought back on both modern blockbusters and retro classics to create a definitive ranking of all of Rockstar’s open-world crime games and determine which GTA game is the best.

After having already made the switch to 3D, Grand Theft Auto: Advance returned the series to its top-down roots in 2004 for a Game Boy spinoff. A prequel to the events of Grand Theft Auto 3, GTA: Advance successfully brings the classic car-jacking, crime spree gameplay of the original games to Nintendo’s portable. While there is a story that ties into GTA 3, GTA: Advance is primarily gameplay driven, giving players over 300 missions to complete which makes for a fun excursion but hardly a full GTA experience in the modern sense.

An expansion pack for the original GTA, Grand Theft Auto: London 1969 is notable for taking place in the real city of London as opposed to a fictional amalgam like Los Santos (Los Angeles) or Liberty City (New York City). Like most of the early GTA games, it is hardly recognizable today and is more of a fun retro relic of the past. However, London remains one of the most fan-requested locations for the series to revisit.

Released two years after the first Grand Theft Auto, Rockstar returned with an improved sequel. Set in an almost cyberpunk-ish retro futuristic city, it boasted better graphics and tuned-up gameplay. But this early on in the series, Grand Theft Auto was still mostly about stealing and destroying cars and scoring the most points. One notable thing about GTA 2 was an eight-minute long short movie created by Rockstar that was used as the intro cutscene for the game, hinting at the cinematic direction the series would take later on in the series.

The game that started it all, Grand Theft Auto 1 seems almost unrecognizable from the game series it is today. A top-down, mission-based experience where players steal cars to reach the end of a level, Grand Theft Auto 1 was mostly about running over people and evading cops. While GTA started as an honest-to-goodness car-stealing game, the wanton destruction and irreverent sense of humor was part of the series’ DNA from the very beginning, and these traits would carry on throughout as the series made the jump to 3D.

Grand Theft Auto: Chinatown Wars delves into the world of the Triads, one of the many criminal factions that have appeared on the sidelines throughout the series. It was released during the series’ popularity surge of the PS2 3D era, but opted to resurrect the original top-down design, albeit reinforced by a striking visual design inspired by GTA’s iconic box art. Sticking to tradition, it is yet another story of a small-time con making it big in the criminal underworld, but the main attraction is Chinatown War’s novel use of touch controls.

While Chinatown Wars has since been ported to several handheld consoles including PSP and iOS devices, many agree that the original DS version is the best experience thanks to the fun and unique ways Chinatown Wars utilized Nintendo’s touch screen. Not many other games on Nintendo’s dual-screened system will let you use the screen to hotwire a car.

10. Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories

The first portable 3D GTA game, Liberty City Stories fit Grand Theft Auto 3’s whole open world into a handheld package, without the need to sacrifice ambition and return to the series’ top-down roots. Expanding the world of GTA 3, it features several recurring characters including Salvatore Leone, the Mafia Don who is a primary fixture of Liberty City across numerous games.

9. Grand Theft Auto: The Lost and Damned

The first expansion for Grand Theft Auto 4, The Lost and the Damned stars biker gang member Johnny and takes place during the events of the base game. While the story isn’t the most memorable, The Lost and the Damned adds more weapons and vehicles to GTA 4, making the large game feel even bigger. Along with The Ballad of Gay Tony, The Lost and the Damned was an important exploration into episodic storytelling for Rockstar, something that would be recontextualised with its frequent GTA Online updates.

Grand Theft Auto 3 took the GTA series into the third dimension, taking the formerly top-down, level-based game, and turning it into the third-person, open-world series we know today.

Telling the story of two-bit criminal Claude and his rise in the criminal world of Liberty City, GTA 3 was the foundation upon which all future GTA games would be built on. Riffing on the likes of The Sopranos and Goodfellas, it established the cinematic ambitions that would fuel Rockstar for the next two decades. Grand Theft Auto 3 hasn’t aged as well as some of the studio’s other early games, but it remains a foundational text for the future of the series.

The second handheld GTA game for the PSP, Vice City Stories returns to Rockstar’s version of Miami for a prequel to the 1980s-set PS2 hit. Playing as Vic, the brother of Vice City’s Lance Vance, you build up a criminal empire by wresting control of establishments and organizations from rival criminal gangs. Along with huge technical improvements over the first PSP game, Liberty City Stories, the main drawback in 2006 was being able to play a fully-fledged, 3D GTA game on the go, complete with a fresh new 1980s soundtrack and Phil Collins in-game cameo.

The real reason why we likely haven’t received GTA 6 sooner, GTA Online was initially a multiplayer side component to GTA 5 before taking on a life of its own. While on the surface it is a free-for-all sandbox set in Los Sanos, GTA Online is effectively a reincarnation of Second Life only with more car races and explosions.

Players can join up together with friends to take part in the addictingly fun heists, but just as easily screw around the world, flying around in jetpacks, or crashing airplanes into each other. GTA Online has also developed a robust role-playing community where players can live out the best (or worst) versions of themselves in a self-contained online world.

5. Grand Theft Auto 4: The Ballad of Gay Tony

The second DLC expansion for Grand Theft Auto 4, The Ballad of Gay Tony takes place alongside the events of the main game but expands upon the gameplay in key ways. Playing as former drug dealer Luis, who Niko crossed paths with in the main campaign, you’re able to manage “Gay” Tony Prince’s night clubs, an activity that will return in Grand Theft Auto Online later on. Largely considered one of the best DLCs of its era, its plot tied up all the loose threads of the GTA 4 story in a satisfying way.

As the first high-definition Grand Theft Auto game, GTA 4 was a massive leap for Rockstar in terms of its technical prowess. However, the biggest advancement in GTA 4 was its cinematic storytelling style. The story of Eastern European immigrant Niko Bellic, one of GTA’s best protagonists, is a surprisingly dark and cutting satire of the American dream.. In our original review, we called it an “Oscar-caliber drama” and the movie quality storytelling would only become better in the sequel, GTA 5. Of course, Niko’s adventures in Liberty City are best remembered for all the times he went bowling with his disastrous cousin, Roman – the result of a dynamic social system in which friends and allies would call you up perhaps a little bit too often.

San Andreas and GTA 5 may have overshadowed Grand Theft Auto: Vice City in terms of scale, but Rockstar’s sendup to Miami Vice and Scarface remains one of the most stylish entries in the series. Set in the fictionalized version of Miami, Vice City stars Tommy Vercetti’s career criminal, voiced by the iconic Ray Liotta, as he sets out to make a name for himself after getting released from prison. The vibrant storytelling and setting of Vice City showed Rockstar was more than just the makers of extremely violent games, they were makers of extremely violent games that were also cool as hell.

Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas was a turning point for the series, adding many of the deep customization options and rich systems the series has since become known for. Starring gang member Carl “CJ” Johnson, San Andreas follows his return to Los Santos after spending five years in Liberty City, and how he ends up getting dragged into a broader gang battle over the many territories around San Andreas.

At the time, IGN called it “the single best PlayStation 2 title” we ever played with production values that were “second to none.” Along with taking the series to the west coast for the first time with a map that sprawled over no fewer than three cities, San Andreas featured the best GTA story to-date, a rich customization system for CJ, an expanded money system with dozens of shops to spend it in, numerous minigames, and a dynamic gang wars system, all of which combined into one of the most fully-featured GTA games ever.

Over the decades Rockstar has continuously improved its storytelling ambitions and open-world complexity, and it all led to Grand Theft Auto 5. Although it was first released in 2013 for the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360, GTA 5 has since been re-released for each successive PlayStation and Xbox system, as well as PC; each time subtly enhanced and each time selling millions of more copies.

Primarily a story of a criminal crew comprising Michael De Santa, Trevor Philips, and Franklin Clinton, the reason for GTA 5’s continued popularity is the sheer scale of its central setting, Los Santos, where players can freely explore the vast open world to their hearts desires. In IGN’s perfect 10 review, we praised the “extraordinary scope” of GTA 5 and fell in love with its “living world where anything can happen.” It is the current pinnacle of everything Rockstar set out to achieve with the series, featuring one of the largest, most detailed open-world maps in gaming, boundless activities — from skydiving to street racing — and an engrossing, cinematic story.

This is our ranking of the best Grand Theft Auto games of all time. Let us know in the comments which ones were your favorites, and be sure to check out our full coverage of Grand Theft Auto 6 including 99 details you may have missed from the first trailer.

Matt T.M. Kim is IGN's Senior Features Editor. You can reach him @lawoftd .

articles.title: Sundance 2026’s Most Buzzed About Film Is Finally in Theaters This Weekend
articles.summary: Josephine Review: Sundance 2026’s most buzzed about film is a stunning drama about an eight-year-old witnessing a violent crime.
articles.body:
Josephine is in select theaters on Nov. 20. This review is based on a screening from the Sundance Film Festival.

Beth de Araújo’s Josephine — which won both the Grand Jury Prize at Sundance as well as the festival’s Audience Award — is as visceral as it is delicate. The story of an eight-year-old girl who witnesses a violent sexual assault, and her parents who don’t quite know how to help her cope, the movie’s difficult story, and its rough, raw aesthetic approach, create some of the most challenging parameters for a child actress in recent memory. However, the young performance at its center is as miraculous as the film that slowly coheres around it, resulting in a freight train of emotional impact.

Early one morning in San Francisco, when Josephine (Mason Reeves) and her father Damien (Channing Tatum) go running in Golden Gate Park, they’re briefly separated, and the second grader watches from afar as a mysterious assailant in a green t-shirt (Philip Ettinger) overpowers and assaults an unsuspecting jogger (Syra McCarthy). In a horrifying moment, both victim and perpetrator lock eyes with the young girl, before the attack is broken up and the man is chased and arrested. However, neither Damien nor his wife Claire (Gemma Chan) can decide on the right way to explain to Josephine what she saw, leaving her emotionally adrift as she grows more confused, more resentful of authority, and more violent towards her classmates. As the days go by, she even begins picturing the attacker in the spaces around her — even in the safety of her bedroom.

De Araújo’s frank, unflinching approach to this event stems from having witnessed exactly such an attack at a similar age, imbuing Josephine with an autobiographical quality. Its contours are gradually shaped by the parent characters, and their expertly rendered performances, which lean into Tatum and Chan’s broad types in pursuit of unexpected layers. Damien, although playful at times, is a tough-love kind of parent whose words fail him, but who demands a stiff upper lip from Josephine while trying to navigate the event and its legal aftermath (the victim moves away, leaving Josephine as the only eye witness). Tatum’s comedy has often tapped into a meathead, frat boy persona, and de Araújo’s film is no different, only it captures the difficult domestic eventuality of that masculine mode in the form of a father whose solution to helping his daughter understand the world is stern silence and self-defense classes.

Chan’s gracefulness, on the other hand, informs Claire’s approach in discomforting ways as well. A dancer and an artist, she searches for ways to talk Josephine through this trauma, but falls back on platitudes, and can’t find ways to answer her daughter when she inevitably asks if she’s ever been a victim of a similar assault. There’s no prescribed perfect age for sex education, and certainly none for explaining, to a pre-adolescent, the grey areas of human sexuality — the attacker’s defense attorneys claim the encounter was consensual non-consent — let alone the definition of “rape.” There’s certainly no handbook for what to do when the ideal time for this discussion slips into the past, for reasons beyond a parent’s control. But unlike Claire and Damien, who each fall back on their own parents’ imperfect, cyclical approaches to supposedly taboo topics, Josephine has the internet at her disposal, though the explanations she finds online only confuse her further.

Reeves, who de Araújo discovered at a farmer’s market a few months before filming, brings a shocking naturalism to the part. Josephine is the masculine “Jo” to her father, and the cutesy “JoJo” to her mother, roles which the character and the actress alike effortlessly oscillate between, as they try to find a sense of stability while the floor is pulled out from under them. Josephine’s growing unease is reflected in daring fashion by the young newcomer, whose growing uncertainty — surrounding both human sexuality and human morality — seeps into her mood in the form of subdued frustrations. Reeves holds these close to the chest, until they eventually boil over. She’s practically a ticking time bomb; it’s as magnificent a debut performance as you’ll ever see.

These emotional pieces are all fitted into place by de Araújo’s deft and careful hand, yielding a film with a psychological complexity (surrounding issues of childhood sexual trauma) on the level of Gregg Araki’s Mysterious Skin. The director’s conception of San Francisco adds to the imposing nature of the story, between its winding streets and the crisscrossing power lines and metal bridge beams that seem to press down on the characters from above. The camera weaves in and out of Josephine’s point of view as though the young girl were being pulled outside herself before being pushed back in, an emotional whiplash further stoked by the use of space. For the most part, de Araújo and cinematographer Greta Zozula place us at eye level and employ telephoto lenses to blur the details of the larger, more imposing adult world in unbroken takes that build in pressure, as though Josephine’s purview were slowly being enveloped by fog. The color green begins to enter her field of view more and more, and eventually, the filmmakers break from their aforementioned blurry approach — with wide lenses that expand space and warp movement — during brief, imaginative moments when Josephine starts to picture the green-shirted attacker in her bedroom, as a specter of the confusion growing in her mind.

Ettinger plays this imagined version of the character with care and caution. He is, at times, an imposing presence, but he can also be ghostly and melancholic, almost sympathetic. He raises questions of what his eyes meeting with Josephine’s in the park may have done to her, and the ways in which her interpretation of the event — and of what led to it — might be forced to change over time as well, when her parents can’t seem to figure out how to connect with her long enough to comfort her. This moment of primal identification with the rapist causes her to turn inward, and to wonder whether she herself has the capacity for evil. That she begins to wear green nail polish goes unremarked upon, but it’s one of the film’s many stark, unmissable details that might cause you to squirm in your seat.

The movie nestles broad philosophical questions within the perspective of a child, which — in tandem with Miles Ross’ brilliantly breathy and propulsive score — inject a terrifying undercurrent into moments of dramatic simplicity. This is centered around the magic of a young performer guiding us through the story’s silent developments by getting lost in thought and self-loathing, and the adult characters who aren’t emotionally equipped to meet her gaze. All this combined makes Josephine one of the most powerful, shattering works of drama to emerge from the modern American independent scene.

articles.title: Among the Bluejays Walkthrough - Enshrouded Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Among the Bluejays is a main quest in Enshrouded that sends you on a mission to unlock the best glider in the game—the Ghost Glider. If you are
articles.body:
Among the Bluejays is a main quest in Enshrouded that sends you on a mission to unlock the best glider in the game—the Ghost Glider. If you are wondering how to unlock or complete the Among the Bluejays quest so you can get the coveted Ghost Glider, you'll find everything you need in this Enshrouded guide.

The Among the Bluejays quest is given to you by the Alchemist . To trigger it, you need to complete the Sun Temple Stories quest and speak to the Alchemist. Select the Above and Beyond dialogue option to start Among the Bluejays, and set off toward your new glider!

Among the Bluejays is not an easy quest. It takes place in the Kindlewastes, one of the hardest regions in the game, and it involves completing a series of tricky puzzles. To get started, open your map and plot a course for the Sun Temple in the bottom right corner of the map, almost directly south from the Kindlewastes Ancient Spire.

To reach your destination, fast travel to the Kindlewastes Ancient Spire and jump off the southern side of the tower. Glide as far south as you can and continue running in that direction once you land to find another Sun Temple.

This Sun Temple is heavily guarded, so you have a choice to make. You can run in through the main gate and defeat all enemies in your path, or sneak around the right side of the building. If you sneak around to the right, you only have to defeat one enemy—the one guarding the front door.

Whatever path you choose to take, make your way to the front door. You will realize, however, that the door is locked. You need to hit three switches to open it.

The first button is on the left side of the door.

The second button is on the back of the archway in front of the door.

The third button is on the right side of the door.

Head in the front door once it's open and proceed up the first set of stairs. There are a few enemies here, so take care of them before heading up the next staircase at the back of the room. This is where things get a little tricky. There are four more buttons you need to find, and they aren't as easy to spot as the first three.

Run along the room, keeping a close eye on the inside wall. Eventually, you will spot a hole. Aim your bow through there to hit the first button.

From there, turn right, and head outside the door that leads outside. The next button is on the side of the building out there.

Head back inside and work your way around the room until you see the locked door with four buttons on top. On a pillar to the left of that is a bookcase with the button behind it. Interact with the bookcase to move it and push the button.

The last button is opposite the trap that releases fire balls. Head over there and look up at the top of the wall that the fireballs hit. Shoot the button with an arrow and head through the now-open door to start your climb. Run up the staircases to eventually find yourself outside. Keep heading up the stairs until you encounter some flying enemies and a grapple point. Defeat the enemies and grapple over the gap to find yet another staircase.

This staircase leads you to a locked door. Craft a lockpick to get inside and climb the grate to reach a ledge on the right side of the room. Climb the wooden platform and grapple to the highest point of the tower, where you will find a chest containing the Ghost Glider.

Opening this chest earns you the best glider in the game and completes the Among the Bluejays quest!

articles.title: Barber Needs Shelter Walkthrough - Enshrouded Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Barber Needs Shelter is an Enshrouded quest that tasks you with providing shelter for your Barber so they can operate to their full potential. If you're
articles.body:
Barber Needs Shelter is an Enshrouded quest that tasks you with providing shelter for your Barber so they can operate to their full potential. If you're wondering what exactly constitutes 'shelter' and how to create it, we've got everything you need to know in this Enshrouded guide.

So you've successfully completed the Illuminate The Night quest and got yourself a Barber to spice up your base. But the Barber can't operate properly without some shelter! The first thing you need to get started is some sort of room. You will probably already have a decent base going by the time you rescue the Barber.

The lands are full of ruins in Enshrouded, and if you don't have enough materials to craft a base from scratch, those places offer excellent base opportunities. Many of them will only require a little patching up, and they are good to go! Rookmore and Long Keep are great first base options!

If you're making a base or house for the Barber from scratch, your first stop should be the workbench. There, you can craft building materials that you can use to create walls, floors, windows, and doors for your structure. Then, equip your Construction Hammer and select a floor tile. Lay out a base in whatever shape feels good for you, then craft some walls to border it.

Place a roof on top to complete your building. It doesn't even need a door to count as shelter, although adding one is a good idea. Once your structure is complete, craft a bed to place in there. The most basic bed option is the Crude Mattress, which you can craft using the following materials:

4x Torn Cloth: Found by defeating enemies.

4x Plant Fiber: Gathered from bushes and shrubbery.

Place your bed inside the structure, then use your Summoning Staff to summon the Barber to the area. Click on the bed to assign it to him and complete your quest!

articles.title: Ignite the Coldest Elixir Well Walkthrough - Enshrouded Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Ignite the Coldest Elixir Well is an Enshrouded quest that sends you into the heart of the Albaneve Summits to clear three Shroud Roots inside a remote cavern.
articles.body:
Ignite the Coldest Elixir Well is an Enshrouded quest that sends you into the heart of the Albaneve Summits to clear three Shroud Roots inside a remote cavern. The cavern entrance itself is pretty tough to find, as are the Shroud Roots inside, so if you're looking for some tips, you'll find everything you need in this Enshrouded guide.

The Elixir Well you're looking for is hidden deep in the Shroud just north of the Albaneve Summits tower. To reach it, fast travel to the Albaneve Summits Ancient Spire and jump off the northeastern side to the path below. Start following the path until you reach the Shroud.

Follow the path until it branches, then take the path leading left . Continue following the path once it branches, and you will eventually find yourself at a large, stone bridge. Make your way over the bridge and continue down the path to reach a large stone building that marks the entrance to the Elixir Well.

You will be met with enemies as soon as you reach the Elixir Well entrance. You can either take the time to knock each and every one of them out or just ignore them if you're concerned about running out of time in the Shroud.

Keep heading straight forward through the stone tunnel, keeping your eyes on the ground as you go. There's a hole in the ground about halfway down the hall with a chest inside, so pick that up before continuing on.

Eventually, you will find yourself at a dead end. Glide off the edge of the path and head straight forward, over some wooden structures and under some large, stone archways. Once you reach land on the other side, you will spot the first Shroud Root, along with a horde of enemies. Pick off the enemies around you to clear your way to the Shroud Root and start cutting it down with an axe. With the first Shroud Root taken care of, you'll be free to move on to the next one.

Make your way west to find a wooden platform leading to an air current. Glide off the edge and use the current to fly straight toward the second Shroud Root. Clear the surrounding bugs, cut that Shroud Root down, and turn east to spot a grapple point in the distance. Use your Grapple Hook to reach the upper level and head straight toward the third Shroud Root.

You will get a Fell Cyclops Head for defeating the monster, which you can use to upgrade your flame, a Shroud Nexus, some other items, and a Cyclops Torso piece, which you can use to complete the A Skeleton Cyclops Collection quest for the Collector. With that taken care of, head over to the Shroud Root and chop it down to complete the Ignite the Coldest Elixir Well quest!

articles.title: Férias, alistamento militar e 'viagem falsa' à Nova Zelândia: as loucuras que fãs de 'GTA 6' estão fazendo pelo lançamento | G1

articles.summary: A Sensor Tower estima que o jogo já arrecadou US$ 1,18 bilhão, o equivalente a R$ 6,84 bilhões, em pré-vendas nas plataformas PlayStation e Xbox.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto 6 terá uma personagem feminina jogável pela primeira vez — Foto: Rockstar Games/Divulgação via BBC

Os fãs de Grand Theft Auto esperaram longos 13 anos pelo lançamento da edição mais recente do jogo — e estão fazendo de tudo para se preparar para a estreia.

GTA 6 será lançado na quarta-feira (18/11), e Victoria Evans, de West Sussex, na Inglaterra, não está deixando nada ao acaso. Ela programou o despertador para acordar de madrugada e reservou um dia de folga no trabalho.

Evans contou à BBC que incluiu o lançamento do jogo no formulário de solicitação de férias, que foi aprovado, apesar de seu chefe "não saber o que é GTA 6 ".

Ela está longe de ser a única. Para o dia do lançamento do jogo, a empresa de software de recursos humanos BrightHR analisou dados de ausências de mais de 1,2 milhão de funcionários de 70 mil empresas em todo o Reino Unido.

O levantamento constatou que GTA foi mencionado em 4,6% dos pedidos de folga feitos pelos funcionários. Ao longo de novembro e dezembro, estima-se que 83 mil dias de folga tenham sido reservados por causa do jogo.

E tirar um dia de folga é apenas uma das maneiras pelas quais os fãs estão se preparando para a grande estreia. Outros estão comprando um novo console para jogar ou até fingindo estar do outro lado do mundo para conseguir acesso antecipado.

A empresa de inteligência de mercado Sensor Tower estima que GTA 6 já tenha gerado US$ 1,18 bilhão (R$ 6,84 bilhões) com 12 milhões de cópias vendidas na pré-venda — embora a Rockstar, empresa por trás do jogo, não tenha confirmado esses números.

Apesar da possibilidade de baixar antecipadamente os 212 GB do jogo, Jennifer Holmes, diretora-executiva da London Internet Exchange, afirmou que vários provedores de internet do Reino Unido, incluindo BT e Virgin Media, haviam "ampliado sua capacidade em antecipação a uma demanda maior" antes do lançamento.

Os jogadores já são conhecidos por tirar dias de folga do trabalho para acompanhar grandes lançamentos.

Quando Red Dead Redemption 2 foi lançado, em outubro de 2018, usuários das redes sociais compartilharam seus planos de faltar ao trabalho.

Na época, uma empresa de análise de dados teria constatado que mais pessoas falavam em alegar doença para faltar ao trabalho por causa do jogo do que por qualquer outro título naquele ano.

Conversas semelhantes ocorreram antes do lançamento de Cyberpunk 2077 , em dezembro de 2020, quando fãs discutiram a possibilidade de tirar vários dias de folga para jogar.

GTA 6 se passa em um estado fictício inspirado na Flórida — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

Algumas instituições decidiram aproveitar a tendência em torno de GTA 6 e oferecer incentivos relacionados ao jogo — entre elas, a 3ª Divisão de Infantaria do Exército dos Estados Unidos, sediada em Fort Stewart, na Geórgia.

A divisão concedeu a alguns militares da ativa uma licença de quatro dias para jogar assim que o título fosse lançado, em novembro, desde que assinassem um contrato de realistamento de pelo menos dois anos entre 1º de agosto e 12 de novembro.

"A ideia era criar um programa de incentivos diferenciado, conectado aos interesses dos soldados", confirmou à BBC, em agosto, a tenente-coronel Angel Tomko, oficial de relações públicas da divisão.

"Havia 130 soldados elegíveis dentro do batalhão, e 20 escolheram esse incentivo como parte de seu realistamento", disse ela na ocasião.

Além de tirar dias de folga, alguns jogadores também vêm discutindo uma brecha técnica que poderia lhes garantir algumas horas extras de jogo antes de o título ser oficialmente lançado em seus países.

Como GTA 6 será lançado à meia-noite no horário local de cada região, a Nova Zelândia será um dos primeiros lugares onde o jogo estará disponível, já que é um dos primeiros países a chegar à meia-noite devido à sua localização.

Isso levou alguns jogadores a investigar maneiras de "enganar" seus consoles, fazendo-os acreditar que estão na Nova Zelândia, quando, na verdade, estão a milhares de quilômetros de distância.

Segundo o Google Trends, as buscas por "truque da Nova Zelândia para GTA 6" aumentaram mais de 5.000% no Reino Unido ao longo do último mês.

A jornalista especializada em videogames Vic Hood disse que muitos jogadores vão querer começar a jogar mais cedo para "participar o quanto antes", além de evitar spoilers .

"Como a Nova Zelândia está 13 horas à frente do Reino Unido, são 13 horas de jogo que podem circular pela internet e potencialmente revelar momentos importantes da história e surpresas dentro do jogo", afirmou.

Isso também significa que os jogadores poderiam começar a jogar em um horário muito mais agradável, às 11h no Reino Unido, em vez de precisarem ficar acordados a noite inteira.

Mas outro usuário do Xbox fez um alerta no Reddit. Ele observou que, embora essa brecha tenha sido explorada durante muitos anos em lançamentos de outros jogos, GTA 6 "pode ser o jogo que finalmente fará a Microsoft tomar alguma providência contra essa 'exploração' do sistema" — o que poderia incluir o banimento de jogadores.

A Rockstar, desenvolvedora de GTA 6, e a Take-Two Interactive, sua distribuidora, não comentaram a brecha. Sony e Microsoft também não se pronunciaram.

Louise Wooldridge, da Ampere Analysis, afirmou que tanto a Microsoft quanto a Sony têm "regras que regem as contas e as compras em diferentes regiões" para Xbox e PlayStation, acrescentando que as regras da Sony são "um pouco mais restritivas".

Assim, os jogadores que optarem por usar essa alternativa podem correr o risco de violar os termos e condições das plataformas e, potencialmente, sofrer restrições em suas contas ou perder o acesso aos jogos digitais.

A expectativa em torno do jogo tomou conta de locais em todo o mundo, incluindo a loja de departamentos Selfridges, em Londres — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

Alguns jogadores terão de esperar ainda mais do que aqueles que jogam em consoles para ter acesso a GTA 6 , já que o título não estará disponível para computador no lançamento, seguindo o padrão de versões anteriores da série.

"Usuários de PC terão de se contentar em acompanhar indiretamente a experiência por meio de vídeos de outras pessoas no YouTube e transmissões na Twitch", disse o jogador Stephen Finn à BBC.

Um PS5 custa atualmente a partir de R$ 4.599,90 no Brasil, enquanto o modelo mais potente, PS5 Pro, sai por R$ 7.499,90.

Apesar do preço elevado, para alguns, a tentação de participar da comunidade que vai jogar aquele que muitos consideram o maior lançamento de videogame do ano, se não da década, foi grande demais.

Publicações no Reddit e vídeos, como o do youtuber americano Isoish, mostram fãs comprando consoles especificamente para jogar o título. "Então, o único jogo que vou ter aqui é GTA ", disse o criador de conteúdo no vídeo. "O PS5 inteiro é para GTA 6 ."

Depois de mais de uma década de espera, alguns fãs parecem determinados a não desperdiçar nem um minuto do lançamento de GTA 6 — independentemente do custo ou do esforço extra.

articles.title: The Macro Is World of Warcraft: Forever’s Accessibility Secret Weapon
articles.summary: The tiny-but-mighty macro keyboard shortcut in World of Warcraft: Forever has proven the perfect accessibility tool.
articles.body:
It’s rare that I can confidently say I’ve never played a specific game or series. Grand Theft Auto, Fire Emblem, The Last of Us Part 2, and, until very recently , World of Warcraft either never piqued my interest or were simply too inaccessible for me to enjoy. With World of Warcraft: Forever , I’m finding it to be one of my favorite gaming experiences of 2026.

I’m no stranger to the MMO genre. I’ve played Final Fantasy 14, Star Wars: The Old Republic, DC Universe Online, Guild Wars 2, and continue to maintain a RuneScape subscription. I’ve always enjoyed the ease of access and design practices of MMOs, but want to acknowledge that older games in the genre tend to suffer the most in terms of inaccessibility. Yet, since creating my first WoW character during Forever’s launch, I’ve been enamored with its overall accessibility. For this Access Designed , let’s explore what I look for in MMO accessibility, and how Forever mostly succeeds.

For approximately 20 years, I’ve enjoyed MMOs in varying ways. Whether endlessly grinding skills on RuneScape, actively running dungeons and slaying world bosses in Guild Wars 2, or heavily investing in my Jedi’s story in SWTOR, MMOs are my second favorite genre, immediately behind turn-based RPGs. In a sense, like RPGs, MMOs have generally been accessible with their options and designs. And as my disease progressed, and my range of motion and energy levels diminished, I was able to find unique ways to continue playing.

Every MMO I’ve played has offered some iteration of customizable controls. When I was younger, I had the capability to reach further across my keyboard, meaning I only needed to customize keybinds for actions beyond the ‘G’ key. Now, with the current progression of my disability, I rely heavily on putting as many functions as possible on my Logitech G903 Lightspeed mouse , since I’m only able to use around three keyboard keys. Thankfully, MMOs, at least those I’ve played, allow you to click each ability on your hot bar.

Old School RuneScape is entirely different, posing its own unique challenges. Every action can be completed through the mouse with the use of a virtual keyboard. This is beneficial for my energy and strength because most actions only require one click, even if it’s leveling combat or skilling around the map. Growing up, RuneScape was by far the most accessible MMO, and remained that way for years, until Jagex released Old School RuneScape in 2013.

Old School RuneScape is essentially RuneScape 2 before Jagex redefined the game with its Evolution of Combat update, also in 2013. I never particularly enjoyed RuneScape 3 because it transformed the relatively easy and accessible vibe of the series into a more traditional MMO with hotkeys and extensive moves. With Old School, the traditional mechanics return, albeit with an emphasis on rapidly clicking for newly added bosses and raids. To properly complete these activities, players are expected to swap between their prayers, as well as gear, to effectively mitigate damage. If my energy levels are low, quickly swapping between my inventory and prayer tabs, switching prayers, and equipping new gear, all while simultaneously clicking to avoid area-based attacks is essentially a hard barrier, often resulting in me dying numerous times.

So, where does Forever compare to other MMOs I’ve played? As a WoW first timer, I’m finding my gameplay experience akin to SWTOR and Final Fantasy 14. Hot bars are crucial, and players are expected to dodge or ‘kite’ attacks, especially if enemies use area of effect abilities. The combat is familiar enough where I can confidently engage with the system, but through in-game settings and accessibility options, Forever is quickly becoming one of the most accessible MMOs I’ve played.

Fully customizable controls, settings like auto-run and action-targeting, which assist with selecting enemies based on camera positioning, all make completing quests, exploring the world, and conquering dungeons far easier. And because I’m playing a mage, my character can quickly burst enemies before I’m overwhelmed – although I admittedly still frequently die when swarmed by two or more monsters. Yet, these relatively traditional accessibility tools aren’t what makes Forever so accessible. Instead, I’ve become enamored with WoW’s acceptance of macros.

At the most basic definition, macros are in-game scripts that apply to varying commands. Movement, skilling, and especially combat can all be modified to simplify gameplay or create a unique rotation that ultimately benefits the player. SWTOR outright bans their use, and Final Fantasy 14 allows macros, though I stopped playing before learning about their use, meaning that Forever is my first proper introduction of this feature. For my mage, I created two macros – one that combines three spells into a single rotation on my ‘F’ key, and one that allows me to cast ‘polymorph’ just by hovering my mouse over an enemy, rather than specifically targeting them. By themselves, these two macros save me so much energy just by reducing how many keys or clicks I need to play. And as I level and unlock more spells and skills, I’m sure I will add more macros to my repertoire.

Beyond the options and design practices I use for my character, I’m just really enjoying playing with my friends. An often-unexplored accessibility concept is playing with others. For me, with my physical disability, questing, exploring, and finishing dungeons is vastly easier when done with a group that understands my limitations and needs. If a quest requires specific loot from an enemy, my friends don’t mind killing the monsters for me, with me looting the bodies afterward. If I’m tired of navigating the map, my friends are always happy to let me automatically follow them to our next destination. With dungeons, I need to perform my role as DPS, but if I die from being too tired or not reacting fast enough, there’s never any conflict. These experiences make navigating Forever so enjoyable. While I love playing solo, I’m always excited to hop on with friends.

Forever is by no means the most accessible game of 2026. In fact, I would argue it’s not the most accessible game of the past five years. Yet, in an industry that constantly tries to outperform each game with flashy new settings or designs, Forever’s success comes from its simplicity. No option is new or groundbreaking, just perfected within the MMO environment. Could Forever use more settings or designs? Absolutely. Will its lack of innovation prevent me from reaching max level and exploring endgame content? Absolutely not.

Grant Stoner is a disabled journalist covering accessibility and the disabled perspective in video games. When not writing, he is usually screaming about Pokémon or his cat, Goomba on Twitter.

articles.title: Nearly Half of Polled IGN Readers Are Taking Time Off to Play GTA 6
articles.summary: IGN has conducted a poll on if our readers would be taking time off to play GTA 6, and nearly half of them said yes.
articles.body:
IGN has conducted a poll on if our readers would be taking time off to play GTA 6 , and nearly half of them said yes.

We are officially less than a week away from the release of GTA 6, which means fans are preparing their launch plans as we speak. Economists have estimated that the U.S. economy will incur a $1 billion loss in productivity when the game launches on Thursday due to people calling out sick. We asked IGN readers if they will be part of that drop in productivity , and it seems like a significant amount of them will be.

The poll had three options, two of which allowed fans to choose whether or not they'd be using PTO or calling in sick on the day of release. The third choice were for users who plan to go into work on November 19. At the time of writing, over 39,000 users have voted, and 46.5% of them stated that they would be taking the day off to play GTA 6 using either PTO or by calling in sick at launch, while 53.3% stated that they wouldn't be taking time off.

The full break down for each poll option is as follows:

Are IGN Readers Taking Time Off to Play GTA 6?

Yes, I am requesting/have already requested PTO - 38.3%

Yes, but I am calling sick on the day of release - 8.2%

GTA 6 is expected to have one of the largest entertainment launches of all time and will likely shatter GTA 5's records. Rockstar set new records in 2013 for having the fastest entertainment product to hit $1 billion, with $815 million of that coming in the first day. Given GTA 6 will actually cost more than GTA 5 ($80 for the standard version, $100 for the ultimate edition), it wouldn't be surprising if Rockstar blows way past that. The game has also managed to earn some early praise, as GTA 6 is nominated for eight awards at The Game Awards , including the highly sought-after Game of the Year trophy.

To make sure fans are aware of the cultural juggernaut's looming release, Rockstar has been turning Miami into Vice City in real life . The city is currently plastered with in-universe ads for GTA brands, with GTA-branded cars driving all over the place , a Vice City blimp flying over it, and the Miami Heat's arena has even been decked out with Vice City signage. Rockstar also paid $975,000 to install a neon pink sign that reads "Welcome to Vice City." Tomorrow, Rockstar will sponsor a regular season Miami Heat game and turn the team into the Vice City Heat with new jerseys and a never-before-seen court.

The game is less than 24 hours from beginning its regional roll out, starting with New Zealand . With all of that said, if you're one of the people skipping work or school play, make sure you pre-load the game so you don't waste a second of your precious time off downloading the game. And while you wait, be sure to check out our interviews with various content creators to see how they're preparing for this gargantuan launch , as well as community members who are preparing to say goodbye to GTA 5 .

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

Following announcements from Nintendo and PlayStation, Xbox has officially revealed the details of its Black Friday sale.

Deals go live on November 19 — this Friday — at 9am PST. The big headliner is up to 80% digital Xbox and PC games, with additional discounts on Xbox accessories, including custom engraved controllers. What there’s no mention of, though? Consoles.

Xbox was kind enough to offer a sneak peek of the over 2,000 games that will go on sale. These are digital-only deals, but we’re keeping an eye out for physical game deals at Amazon and Best Buy .

Fresh discounts on 2026 releases include 30% off Gears of War: E-Day, 25% off Forza Horizon 6, and for the sports-inclined, 55% off NBA 2K27 and 50% off Madden NFL 27. Final Fantasy VII Remake Integrate, Crimson Desert, The Blood of Dawnwalker, and Halo: Campaign Evolved will also go on sale.

A selection of Xbox controller discounts are already available through the Xbox direct store, and it’s unclear whether those prices will be dropping any further. XBOX Wireless Gaming Controller | Shock Blue

Finally, Xbox is collaborating with Samsung on its Black Friday bundle. Nope, it doesn’t include any games or consoles. Instead, the bundle feels like a lingering remnant of the controversial "Everything Is an Xbox" campaign, which was technically retired soon after Asha Sharma was named CEO . Nonetheless, for Black Friday 2026, eligible Samsung TVs will come with Xbox’s new Nano controller and two months of Game Pass Ultimate.

So, what’s going on with the consoles? Well, it’s not just Xbox. We already knew that PlayStation is skipping out on the console deals this year , just as both systems are getting the biggest game launch of all time. ( GTA 6 , in case that wasn’t clear).

Unfortunately, we’re in the thick of RAMageddon , an ongoing memory shortage that has contributed to supply issues and price hikes across the console and tech space. articles.title: Robert Pattinson's James Bond Casting Process Details Revealed by Amazon's Jeff Bezos
articles.summary: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, who purchased MGM Studios in 2022 and assumed full control over the James Bond 007 franchise last year, shared details on the casting process and how the creative leads, including the director of the next 007 film Denis Villeneuve, ended up choosing The Batman and The Odyssey actor Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond.
articles.body:
Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, who purchased MGM Studios in 2022 and assumed full control over the James Bond 007 franchise last year, shared details on the casting process and how the creative leads, including the director of the next 007 film Denis Villeneuve, ended up choosing The Batman and The Odyssey actor Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond .

Speaking at an event with media company Semafor, Bezos spoke for a couple of minutes on the Bond casting process (hat tip: Steve Jurvetson ), saying he was "heavily involved" before detailing how it came down to Pattinson. "We ran a really tight process," he said. "We made the final decision on Friday. We down-selected to five finalists and then we did real old-fashioned screen tests of those five finalists. And it was really interesting. Full costume, real sets, other actors with them. We did three different scenes with each of the five finalists and then we got together on Friday to spend a couple of hours looking at all of the screen tests.

"All of the actors were extraordinarily talented. By the time we got to this list of five, they were all amazing. But there was something special about Rob Pattinson and his performances. And it was immediately undebated. Denis, we all gravitated towards Rob."

Bezos and his team did question it for a bit, though. "Initially, I would say we were slightly biased a little against him just because he's already so famous," he explained. "We sort of thought maybe we should have somebody a little more unknown. But in the screening tests it was so obvious: he is James Bond."

Interestingly, after Bezos asked fans who they'd like to see as the next James Bond last year, Superman actor Henry Cavill won the popular vote. Instead, of course, an actor who has played DC's other ultra-famous superhero got the gig. Unfortunately, though, it stands to reason that Pattinson might not continue as Bruce Wayne and Batman after 2028's The Batman Part II.

It's been a heck of a year for Pattinson, certainly, between starring in The Odyssey, Primetime, The Drama, and next month's Dune: Part 3; filming The Batman Part II; and landing the role of Bond.

articles.title: Infinity Nikki Players Baffled After Elon Musk's Mom Appears in Game's Update Trailers
articles.summary: Infinity Nikki players were baffled when Elon Musk’s mother, Maye Musk, appeared in a series of trailers announcing the game’s forthcoming 3.0 update on November 16.
articles.body:
Infinity Nikki players were baffled when Elon Musk’s mother, Maye Musk, appeared in a series of trailers announcing the game’s forthcoming 3.0 update on November 16.

Yep, you read that correctly; Maye Musk appeared as a celebrity guest in commercials for the popular open-world dress-up game Infinity Nikki , which you can watch on the game’s official RedNote account (though you’ll need to make an account to view them). If you weren’t aware of this, you aren’t alone, as it seems that Maye’s advertisements weren’t exactly promoted on the game’s English-language social media profiles — and looking at comments on platforms like Twitter and Reddit, this strategy doesn’t come as a big surprise.

RedNote is a Chinese social media app that's most often compared to TikTok. Infinity Nikki is developed by PaperGames, a studio in mainland China, and boasts a strong fanbase in the country. So does Maye Musk, apparently, judging by the excited remarks on RedNote (a Chinese social app that’s often compared to TikTok).

Maye Musk is something of a celebrity in China. Since at least 2023, the model and famous mum has appeared in all sorts of advertisements and campaigns in the country, representing brands that sell products like makeup, massage devices, and even down jackets, per a report from the New York Times . In that same report, Yang Hu, an expert on China’s beauty industry, explained her popularity: “[Her image] carries an element of successful parenting, attracting a significant number of mothers among her followers.”

These comments are echoed in the remarks that fans left on Billibilli’s live-streamed Infinity Nikki Version 3.0 First-Look Event. Automatic translations show that viewers were equal parts confused and delighted by her appearance as a host, with some writing, “Who the hell?” while others exclaimed, “Bestie, you’ve really made it big!” and, “You’re awesome!”

Given Elon Musk’s controversial nature in the West, comments on English social media sites were decidedly less positive.

“I can't believe what they've done here. I'm in shock. I was so excited to play version 3.0, but now I don't want to play anymore. What were they thinking? Can they genuinely recover from this?” one user wrote on Reddit.

“I’m out. That’ll teach me to sink money into a game. I literally justified the spending because I wanted to get a mental break away from these bulls**t people,” another said .

“I was thinking about trying this game. Now I certainly won't,” yet another admitted .

Overall, this particular advertising blitz seems to have put a sour taste in Western players’ mouths, but, perhaps even more curiously, has exposed the vast differences in opinion toward the Musk family between the game’s Eastern and Western communities.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: GTA 6 Fans Baffled After Jason's Actor Gets Left Out of Game Awards Nominations
articles.summary: GTA 6 fans are a bit surprised that the actor playing Jason wasn't nominated at The Game Awards.
articles.body:
GTA 6 fans are a bit surprised that the actor playing Jason wasn't nominated at The Game Awards.

Earlier today, The Game Awards gave us our first indicator of how GTA 6 will be received. It's up for eight awards, including Game of the Year . It was a bit odd, as there are no reviews for the game at the moment, but the jury clearly deemed it worthwhile. The other notable thing to come out of the Game Awards nominations was that it confirmed the actress for Lucia: Manni L. Perez . Fans have speculated she was Lucia for years now, but now it's confirmed, as she was nominated for Best Performance.

However, the actor who plays the game's other protagonist was not nominated. Fans were taken aback, since the two are clearly a package deal in the game, and one has to imagine they elevate each other. However, the jury must not have felt strongly enough about Jason to give his actor the nomination. There's no rule against nominating multiple actors for a single project, either. Last year, three performers from Expedition 33 were all nominated in the same category, after all.

Jason has been seen as a much more subtle and reserved character compared to Lucia. He's a bit quieter, isn't too flashy with his actions, and maybe lacks the fire in his character compared to someone like Lucia. One fan on Reddit noted that Jason didn't make a strong impression on them in any of the trailers: "Honestly, I'm not a fan of his VO," they said . "Jason doesn't sound good, at least in the footage we saw; he lacks diction. Most of the time, I can't understand what he's saying without subs."

However, another fan pushed back, noting that other great Rockstar actors have been snubbed in the past: "Benjamin Byron Davis wasn't nominated for his Dutch performance [in Red Dead Redemption 2]," they said . "Didn't take away one bit and [it's] arguably the best performance in the game."

It's certainly a valid point, especially since Rob Wiethoff also wasn't nominated for his role as John Marston in Red Dead Redemption 2, despite being a secondary protagonist. As of right now, we're not sure who is playing Jason, but it won't be long before we find out. GTA 6 will officially go live tomorrow morning in select regions, as the game becomes available in New Zealand . It'll be interesting to see which of the two protagonists fans end up gravitating toward more in the end, but it seems like Lucia may be a favorite based on her nomination.

Imagem de divulgação de GTA VI. — Foto: Reprodução/Rockstar Games

Após 13 anos de espera, o Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) chega aos consoles nesta quinta-feira (19). O jogo da Rockstar Games passou por adiamentos e vazamentos, mas será lançado oficialmente à meia-noite.

O jogo sucede GTA 5, em uma franquia que, segundo a Take-Two, já passou de 475 milhões de cópias vendidas. Abaixo, veja o que você precisa saber sobre o GTA VI:

A estreia está prevista para o PlayStation 5 e o Xbox Series X|S. O lançamento ocorrerá à meia-noite, no horário local de cada região, segundo a empresa. No Brasil, portanto, os jogadores poderão começar a aventura a partir da virada de quarta para quinta-feira.

O game também poderá ser jogado no Xbox One por meio do Xbox Cloud Gaming, serviço de jogos por streaming da Microsoft. Nesse caso, a transmissão estará disponível a partir das 3h da manhã (horário de Brasília) de 19 de novembro.

No Brasil, a edição Standard custa R$ 449,90 e a Ultimate, R$ 549,90, com valores iguais na PlayStation Store e na Microsoft Store. Nos Estados Unidos, as edições custam US$ 79,99 e US$ 99,99.

Inicialmente, GTA 6 terá versões para PlayStation 5 e Xbox Series X|S. Confira as opções:

PlayStation 5: terá versão nativa do jogo.

Xbox Series X|S: também receberá uma versão nativa.

Xbox One: poderá rodar o título por meio do Xbox Cloud Gaming, serviço de jogos por streaming da Microsoft. A transmissão estará disponível a partir das 3h (horário de Brasília) de 19 de novembro. Os gráficos utilizarão as configurações da versão para Xbox Series S.

PC: ainda não tem data de lançamento anunciada pela Rockstar.

O jogo não terá versões nativas para PlayStation 4 ou Xbox One.

O cenário é o estado fictício de Leonida, inspirado na Flórida, e uma das áreas da história é Vice City, que faz referência a Miami e já foi palco do jogo lançado em 2002. Os protagonistas são Jason Duval e Lucia Caminos, um casal no estilo Bonnie e Clyde que o jogador pode controlar.

Na trama, a dupla tenta se misturar em Vice City e juntar dinheiro para escapar da situação depois que um trabalho simples dá errado. Como em GTA 5, será possível alternar entre os dois personagens, a depender do momento da história.

articles.title: Stephen A. Smith defends response to Trump’s claims about helping Black Americans
articles.summary: ESPN commentator Stephen A. Smith defended his decision not to push back on President Trump’s claims about his record with Black Americans during their recent interview, arguing that viewers deserved to hear the president’s full thoughts without constant interruptions. In an interview last week on Smith’s “Straight Shooter” podcast, Trump — who has called Smith…
articles.body:
ESPN commentator Stephen A. Smith defended his decision not to push back on President Trump’s claims about his record with Black Americans during their recent interview, arguing that viewers deserved to hear the president’s full thoughts without constant interruptions.

In an interview last week on Smith’s “Straight Shooter” podcast, Trump — who has called Smith an “arrogant fool” and “low IQ” in the past — touted what he considered to be his administration’s achievements for Black Americans with little pushback from Smith.

“The Black community is the biggest beneficiary of what I’ve done,” Trump said.

Smith addressed the criticism Tuesday on his podcast, saying made the conscious decision to let Trump make his case rather than challenge each claim as it came up.

“Do I challenge him with the litany of questions that I had, that I wanted to address?” Smith asked. “Do I let people hear what that list is, or do I interrupt him?”

“I decided, without trying to let him go on forever, Black folks needed to hear what he believes he has done for our community. And that’s why I let it go, at least to some degree,” he continued.

Smith also argued that pressing Trump on every questionable statement could have derailed the conversation, describing the president as a master at filibustering who “doesn’t hesitate to embellish.”

“You had a lot of people that felt that I should have pushed back more. And I won’t say any names, but particularly people that have been in this industry before, that should understand by now what comes with an interview like that,” he said.

He suggested that some of his critics were more interested in seeing him confront the president than in hearing what Trump had to say.

“You want to engage in looking the part, and looking like you’re pushing back, not recognizing the fact it’s the President of the United States, you’re inside the White House in the Roosevelt Room, and in a nanosecond he could have just got up and walked out,” Smith said.

Smith went on to fact check several of Trump’s claims from the interview, including his assertion that Black Americans had benefited more than any other group from his administration’s policies.

“Now, obviously that’s unverifiable. It’s his opinion,” Smith said, pointing out that the Black unemployment rate stood at 6.6 percent in October, up from 6.2 percent from when Trump returned to office in January 2025.

“And that number alone can’t prove who benefited most,” he added.

articles.summary: Spider Goat Farm is a small lore-based Enshrouded quest that sends you to one of the five goat farms in the Albaneve Summits. Each goat farm has one piece of
articles.body:
Spider Goat Farm is a small lore-based Enshrouded quest that sends you to one of the five goat farms in the Albaneve Summits. Each goat farm has one piece of the Fluffy Set waiting for you, so tracking them all down is well worth your while. If you're looking for more information on where to find the lore page or the Spider goat Farm, you'll find everything you need in this Enshrouded guide.

The first step to finding the Spider Goat Farm is locating the clue that leads the way. You can find it near the Wildwater Basin in the Albaneve Summits. To get there, fast travel to the Albaneve Summits Ancient Spire and glide off the eastern side. Approach the ravine with two wind currents. Drop down to the path below just before you hit the wind currents and follow the road north until you pass a small cottage on the right.

The cottage does have some chests inside, including one behind a hidden door, but you wont find the lore note there. Continue up the path past the cottage until you reach a small scavenger camp with two tents around a large bonfire.

Inside the small tent on the right, you'll find the How Do I Tell the Boss lore page. Reading it will tip you off about the Spider Goat Farm, and place a marker on your map so you know where to find it.

The Little Rock Goat Farm is just across the other side of the Wildwater Basin. The basin is very deep though, so it's easier to get there by fast traveling back to the Albaneve Summits Ancient Spire and jumping off the eastern side again. Instead of dropping down to the road before hitting the updrafts, ride them to reach the opposite side of the ravine.

Then, follow the road north until you reach a scavenger camp with large wooden structures built into a cave on the right side of the road. Clear the scavengers out and explore the back of the cave to find a small path leading northeast.

This road takes you to the level above the farm, but if you mark it on your map, you will be able to glide off the road as you cross over it and drop down to the building below.

Just as the note said, the farm is filled with spiders. Watch your back as you clear them out then look for a square hole in the ceiling with a grapple point in it. Grapple up there to find your treasure: the Fluffy Boots , which are part of the Fluffy Set.

articles.summary: The Cyclops Cave Near Bridge quest in Enshrouded leads you straight into the lair of a fearsome cyclops near Everfore Keep in the Albaneve Summits. If
articles.body:
The Cyclops Cave Near Bridge quest in Enshrouded leads you straight into the lair of a fearsome cyclops near Everfore Keep in the Albaneve Summits. If you're wondering how to reach the cave passage to retrieve the Right Cyclops Arm that you need for A Skeleton Cyclops Collection , you'll find everything you need in this Enshrouded guide.

The Cyclops Right Arm is attached to a cyclops in a cave passage behind Everfore Keep in the Albaneve Summits. To get there, you first need to make your way to Everfore Keep. Fast travel to the Albaneve Summits Ancient Spire and soar off the northeastern side.

Drop down on the path, and start following it. You'll pass through an enshrouded area, the Gateway Outpost "Alba", the eventually find yourself in the Forge of Obsidia.

The Forge of Obsidia is actually the location of another quest, A Blast Furnace for the Blacksmith . Defeat enemies inside the main forge room until one of them drops the Bellows item. Tuck that away in your pack and use it to craft a Blast Furnace for the Blacksmith once you get back to your base!

For now, continue through the Forge by taking the doorway to the right and following that up a set of stairs. Turn left at the top of the stairs to get back outside again. Turn left as soon as you exit the building and continue following the path until you reach a dead-end.

Take a closer look at the cliff on your right to discover a cave entrance and a new path. Follow it until it branches and you can see some steel arches on the right. Take the path leading left, and continue following it to reach Evermore Keep.

Evermore Keep is locked up tight, so sneak around the traps to the locked door on the left and use a Lockpick to open it. Once you're in, head forward and go up the stairs to find yourself in a courtyard. Climb the stairs opposite and run up to a pile of rubble.

Turn left when you reach the rubble and follow the path around the side of the building to reach a grate. Climb the grate and run up the stairs on the left. Work your way around the grounds until you reach a courtyard with stairs leading up the left and right. Run straight up any set of steps and continue north until you reach a dead-end.

Glide off the ledge to reach the enshrouded portion of the building. Head forward into the ruined hall, and climb the stairs on the right to find yourself back outside again. Run straight ahead and turn right at the corner of the building to find a wagon with a grate on the wall beside it.

Climb the grate to find yourself in near a small garden. Head east and look up to your left to spot two grapple points.

These will bring you back out of the shroud. Take the stairs on the northern side of the room, run forward to get back outside, turn right, and right again to reach a large courtyard. Take the stairs on the left and follow them to another courtyard containing a well.

Hook around to your right to climb another small staircase, turn left, and climb the next set. Turn left again to find a large stone archway leading out of Evermore Keep, and follow the road heading northeast. You'll eventually come across a large drop.

Jump and use your grapple hook to swing forward then quickly grab the next grapple point to pull yourself up to the other side. Climb the grate on the left, and continue pushing on.

This leads you to a small cavern on your left and a stack of rubble on your right. Climb the rubble to reach a grapple point on the left. Use that, then turn around and use the second grapple hook to your right. Finally, follow the road to the cyclops cave near the bridge.

There is, of course, a cyclops waiting for you at the end. Defeat it to retrieve the Right Cyclops Arm and get one step closer to finishing A Skeleton Cyclops Collection !

Where to Find the Obsidian Building Blocks in Enshrouded
